title: Jerusalem Artichoke Pancakes
changes_from_base: A savoury grated-vegetable pancake: Jerusalem artichokes and onion bound with egg, a little flour, maple syrup and nut oil, seasoned with cayenne and nutmeg, and fried in oil and butter instead of a poured batter.
summary: Crisp, golden pancakes made from grated Jerusalem artichoke and onion, lightly spiced with nutmeg and cayenne for a warming savoury side.
equipment: 2 baking trays lined with baking paper or foil
food processor with grating disc or box grater
large heavy frying pan or griddle

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Grate
steps.text: Line 2 trays with baking paper or foil. Grate the 2 onions and 1400 g Jerusalem artichokes in a food processor or on a box grater and tip into a large bowl.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk the 2 eggs with the 2 tbsp maple syrup, 2 tbsp walnut or hazelnut oil, 1½ tsp salt, ¼ tsp black pepper, ⅛ tsp cayenne and ¼ tsp nutmeg, then pour over the vegetables and mix lightly with your fingers.

steps.title: Flour
steps.text: Sprinkle the 125 g flour over and mix lightly again.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Shape into 16 pancakes 8 cm across and about 1 cm thick, setting each on a lined tray.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat half the 120 ml vegetable oil and 14 g butter in a large frying pan and cook half the pancakes until golden, 5-7 min a side, lowering the heat if they brown too quickly.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Drain on kitchen paper, then cook the rest in the remaining oil and 14 g butter.

steps.title: Keep
steps.text: Cover loosely with foil and keep warm in a low oven until ready to serve.

tips: Grate the artichokes and onions finely so the pancakes hold together well.
Keep the heat moderate - these brown quickly, so lower it if they colour too fast.
Top up the oil between batches if the pan looks dry.
storage: Keep the cooked pancakes loosely covered with foil in a low oven until ready to serve. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
